s1.syndrome_frame: Sepsis with multiple sites of infection and organ involvement
key_facts: No history or findings suggestive of cirrhosis
Blood and wound cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae
Osteomyelitis in left mid-tibia and right third toe
Increased uptake in right humerus and bilateral femurs on bone scan
Right femur biopsy demonstrated abscess formation

raw.syndrome_frame: Sepsis with multiple sites of infection and organ involvement
key_facts: No history or findings suggestive of cirrhosis
Blood and wound cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae
Osteomyelitis in left mid-tibia and right third toe
Increased uptake in right humerus and bilateral femurs on bone scan
Right femur biopsy demonstrated abscess formation

differentials: Liver abscess due to bacterial infection
per_call: Liver abscess due to bacterial infection

shortlist.label: Pyogenic liver abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a confirmed liver abscess measuring 8.4 × 11 × 13 cm

shortlist.label: Klebsiella pneumoniae infection
shortlist.why_kept: Blood and wound cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, indicating a likely source of sepsis

shortlist.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has osteomyelitis in multiple sites, including left mid-tibia, right third toe, right humerus, and bilateral femurs

shortlist.label: Diabetic foot infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and presents with bilateral lower extremity soft-tissue wounds

shortlist.label: Sepsis due to gram-negative bacteria
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has septic shock and positive cultures for Klebsiella pneumoniae, a gram-negative bacterium

raw.rationale: The presence of Klebsiella pneumoniae in blood and wound cultures, along with the positive string test and the organism's resistance pattern, strongly supports this diagnosis. The patient's clinical presentation, including septic shock and multiple sites of infection (osteomyelitis, liver abscess), is consistent with a systemic Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.

rejected.label: Pyogenic liver abscess
rejected.why: While the patient has a liver abscess, this is one manifestation of a larger systemic infection, which is better explained by the champion diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
rejected.why: The patient's osteomyelitis is part of a broader infectious process, and the term 'chronic' does not capture the acute, systemic nature of the presentation.

rejected.label: Diabetic foot infection
rejected.why: Although the patient has diabetes and foot involvement, the infection is not limited to the feet and involves multiple other sites, suggesting a more systemic process.

rejected.label: Sepsis due to gram-negative bacteria
rejected.why: This diagnosis is correct but less specific than the champion diagnosis, as it does not identify the specific causative organism, Klebsiella pneumoniae.
